## What the plugin is

`RcmdrShinyPlugin.EZR` rebuilds the core clinical-statistics workflow of the
EZR plug-in on top of RcmdrShiny: data preparation, descriptive tables, common
tests, regression, survival analysis, diagnostic accuracy and graphics.

```{r}
remotes::install_github("vigliafg/rstats-commander",
                        subdir = "plugins/RcmdrShinyPlugin.EZR")
RcmdrShiny::run(plugins = "RcmdrShinyPlugin.EZR")
```

EZR replaces the core menus with its own layout.  Load it alone, or last, to keep
the interface predictable.

## Data preparation

- **Variables in active data set** prints the structure of the data.
- **Create dummy variables** expands a factor into indicator columns.
- **Missing observations to a group** turns `NA` into an explicit level.
- **Training-test data split** creates two data sets with a fixed seed.

```{r}
set.seed(123)
.n <- nrow(dataset)
.train <- sample(seq_len(.n), size = floor(0.7 * .n))
train <- dataset[.train, ]
test <- dataset[-.train, ]
```

## Descriptive statistics

- **Summary table of sample characteristics** wraps `tableone::CreateTableOne()`
  and produces the "Table 1" of a clinical paper.
- **Confidence interval for a mean or a proportion** uses the exact dialogs.

```{r}
tableone::CreateTableOne(vars = c("age", "sex"), strata = "group",
                         data = dataset)
```

## Tests

The EZR menu groups the tests by question:

| Question | Dialog |
|---|---|
| Two groups, numeric | Two-sample t-test, Mann-Whitney |
| Paired measurements | Paired t-test, Wilcoxon signed rank |
| Three or more groups | One-way ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis |
| Two categorical variables | Two-way table, McNemar |
| Association between numerics | Pearson, Spearman |

```{r}
t.test(response ~ group, data = dataset, var.equal = FALSE)
wilcox.test(response ~ group, data = dataset)
```

## Regression

```{r}
.model <- glm(outcome ~ age + treatment, data = dataset, family = binomial)
summary(.model)
exp(cbind(OR = coef(.model), confint(.model)))
```

## Survival

Kaplan-Meier and Cox dialogs build `survival::survfit()` and `survival::coxph()`
calls; the log-rank test is included with the Kaplan-Meier output.

## Diagnostic accuracy

ROC curves use `pROC`:

```{r}
.roc <- pROC::roc(outcome ~ marker, data = dataset)
plot(.roc, print.auc = TRUE)
```

Kappa and the two-by-two accuracy table cover agreement and screening tests.

## Limits

This is a core workflow, not a line-by-line port of the 639 menu rows of the
original EZR plug-in.  Meta-analysis, matched-pair analysis, sample-size
calculators and the most advanced survival models remain disabled and are marked
"In porting".
